title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a typed English sheet numbered '-8-', reproduced upside down. It is most likely a sheet of someone else's typescript reused as scrap paper, perhaps the back of a sheet whose other side carries Grothendieck's notes. The surrounding pages (35, 37) are French manuscript computations on hard Lefschetz and Λ-operators for a hyperplane-section or projective-bundle situation φ: Y→X. This typescript is unrelated to them. It belongs to a text on injective sheaves and duality for locally noetherian preschemes. In style and content it matches the 1963–64 Hartshorne seminar on Grothendieck's duality theory (later 'Residues and Duality', Ch. II §7), though that attribution is not certain.

Lemma 3.3: Let A be noetherian, p a prime, I = E(k(p)) the injective hull of the residue field, and X = Spec A. Then Ĩ is injective in the category of all O_X-modules.

Proof as typed:
- Write I as the union of the finite-length A_p-submodules E_i (Matlis: E_i is annihilated by p^i).
- Each Ẽ_i is supported on V(p), the closure of {x}, with sections E_i over every open set containing x.
- So Ĩ = i_{x*}(I), the skyscraper at the (generally non-closed) point x. On the irreducible space V(p) this is the constant sheaf I, extended by 0.
- By adjunction, Hom_{O_X}(F, i_{x*}I) = Hom_{O_{X,x}}(F_x, I).
- Taking stalks is exact and I is injective over A_p, so Ĩ is injective among all O_X-modules.

Proposition 3.4 (statement cut off): On a locally noetherian prescheme, a quasi-coherent F is injective in Mod(O_X) iff F is a direct sum of sheaves J(x) = i_{x*}(E(k(x))). This is the sheaf-theoretic form of the Matlis–Gabriel classification of injectives over noetherian rings. It serves duality theory: dualizing complexes and residual complexes are built from such sheaves (the Cousin complex).
errors: No mathematical errors. 'Constant sheaf I on closure{x}, 0 elsewhere' is correct because closure{x} is irreducible, so every nonempty open subset of it contains x; the sheaf is just i_{x*}I.
The proof uses that I, injective over A and an A_p-module, is injective over A_p = O_{X,x}. This is standard but unstated.
Prop. 3.4 is cut off at the page bottom; its proof is not on this page.

ideas.what: Ĩ for I = E(A/p) is the skyscraper i_{x*}I and is injective in all O_X-modules, via Hom(F, i_{x*}I) = Hom(F_x, I)
